findings.title: All-clients view bypasses an explicit per-client view deny
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel) returns true as soon as canView() is true. canView() is true not only for the view-clients/manage-clients admin roles, but also when a fine-grained permission grants the view scope on the Clients resource type (all clients). The per-client check is then skipped, so a Logic.NEGATIVE view permission for that same caller on one client is never evaluated. requireView(client) and every admin operation gated on canView(client) (client representation, protocol mappers, client scopes) still succeed for the client that was explicitly denied. Negative permissions are already part of this model (user FGAP tests use Logic.NEGATIVE on the same permission API). Short-circuit only on the admin-role helper (canViewClientDefault), then evaluate the per-client decision so an explicit deny overrides all-clients view. The new client tests never create a negative permission, so this bypass is untested.

findings.title: A per-client resource suppresses all-clients permissions
findings.body: hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) loads the authorization resource named with the client id and, if that row exists, evaluates only that resource. The Clients type resource (all clients) is consulted only when no per-client resource exists. A per-client resource is created for any permission that targets that client, including a permission for a different user or a different scope. An administrator granted manage, configure, view, or map-roles on all clients then loses that grant on the client, because their all-clients policy is attached to the type resource and is never evaluated; a per-client grant of scope A also hides an all-clients grant of scope B. Evaluate both resources, and let a per-client policy override all-clients only for the scopes that policy actually covers. PermissionClientTest only covers a lone per-client grant or a lone all-clients grant, never both.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients never receive the Clients schema
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already set, and that is the only place schema scopes and the per-type all-resource records are created. This change adds the Clients resource type and the configure, map-roles-client-scope, and map-roles-composite scopes, but realms that already enabled admin permissions V2 already have that client (created earlier with only Users). After upgrade those scopes and the Clients resource are never inserted, so creating a Clients permission fails with a missing-scope validation error and all-clients evaluation cannot find the type resource. init must add any schema scopes and resource types that are not already present instead of treating a non-null admin-permissions client as fully initialized.

findings.title: Client deletion throws when v1 and v2 admin-permission features are both enabled
findings.body: The removal listener runs when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (v1) is enabled and then calls management().clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. The two flags are independent, so enabling v2 does not turn v1 off. Deleting a client then throws from the provider event listener and can roll back the removal. Guard the v1 cleanup with the same condition management() uses (v1 evaluator actually selected), or make the v2 removal path a no-op instead of throwing. Role and group removal in this listener call management() as well; clients() is the override that now throws.

findings.title: Null Clients type resource NPEs permission checks
findings.body: When no per-client authorization resource exists, hasPermission sets resource from AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource and immediately calls PolicyStore.findByResource(server, resource) with no null check. getResourceTypeResource returns null if the Clients type resource was never created (init skips existing admin-permissions clients) or was deleted. findByResource then dereferences null and the admin call fails with 500 instead of denying the permission. Treat a null type resource as no all-clients permission.

findings.title: Client permission resources are returned with a null display name
findings.body: getResourceName resolves Users policies to "All users" or the username, but has no Clients branch and falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). Per-client resources are stored with the client UUID as the name and no display name, and the all-clients resource is stored as name "Clients" without a display name, so the admin permissions API returns null. The console cannot show which client a permission applies to, unlike users in the same API. Resolve the stored id to the clientId, return a label such as "All clients" for the type resource, and fail clearly if the client no longer exists, matching the user path.

findings.title: canExchangeTo throws instead of returning an authorization decision
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException. AdminPermissions.evaluator installs this class whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, and token exchange calls clients().canExchangeTo to decide whether the caller may exchange into another client's audience. That call now fails the token request with an unhandled server error instead of allow or deny. The same class throws from isPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, and setPermissionsEnabled; this PR only guards the removal listener, and only behind the v1 feature flag. A boolean permission check must not throw — return false until exchange is actually implemented (getEvaluationContext in this class is unused). Otherwise enabling v2 breaks token exchange and any client management-permissions endpoint that still reaches these methods.

findings.title: Client tests rotate myclient's secret and leave realm mutations behind
findings.body: testConfigureOnlyOneClient calls generateNewSecret and invalidateRotatedSecret on myclient and never restores the original secret. realmAdminClient is injected as client myclient using the secret from the realm config, and AbstractPermissionTest's @InjectRealm does not request a per-method lifecycle, so the realm is shared by every method in the class. The next test that must obtain a token authenticates with a secret that no longer exists and fails. The same class also leaves other shared state: testManageOnlyOneClient renames myclient and moves a default client scope to optional, and testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient creates myclient-role and myclient-subRole with no cleanup. AfterEach only deletes scope permissions. Restore the secret, name, and scopes, and delete the roles, or results depend on test order.

findings.title: requireView javadoc claims a boolean result for void methods
findings.body: requireView and requireViewClientScopes are void and throw ForbiddenException when the matching can* check is false, but the new javadoc says each "Returns true if canView()/canViewClientScopes() returns true". That describes the boolean methods, not these require* methods. Neighboring require* docs correctly say they throw ForbiddenException. Callers reading the interface will think these methods return a decision instead of aborting the request.
